skills.name: homelab-intake
skills.description: Use when mapping a homelab for the first time or remapping roles, interfaces, and where Grok Bot should run.
skills.content:
---
name: homelab-intake
description: >-
  Use when mapping a homelab for the first time or remapping roles, interfaces,
  and where Grok Bot should run.
---
Goal: run a short, structured intake that produces a scrubbed lab map and interface recommendations — no secrets, no invented inventory.

## When to use
First real wake after import, or whenever the user asks to remap the lab.

## Steps
1. Ask what exists and what to cover, one cluster at a time (prefer widgets or short questions, not a giant checklist):
   - WAN edge / firewall / router (combined vs split)
   - Managed switches
   - Wi‑Fi controller / APs
   - Hypervisor (Proxmox, ESXi, Hyper-V, Unraid, TrueNAS Scale, etc.)
   - Out-of-band management (iLO, iDRAC, IPMI, BMC)
   - Reverse proxy / web stack
   - Media servers / media library
2. Support vendor variation. Never assume UniFi, Proxmox, or any single brand.
3. Produce a scrubbed map: roles and recommended interfaces only (API/MCP, LAN UI via bot computer, SSH, read-only SNMP). No passwords, no private IPs unless the user pastes them and asks to keep them private in memory (never in a public template).
4. Flag human-gated ops: firmware, WAN/firewall changes, destructive storage, power cycles on OOB.
5. Recommend where to run Grok Bot / bot computers (always-on LAN VM vs workstation vs cloud) given their answers.
6. Propose specialist bots for confirmed roles. Do not CreateAgent until the user confirms the map.

## Guardrails
- Never invent hosts, VLANs, or credentials.
- Never configure live gear during intake.
- Stay quiet on clusters the user skips.

## Plain-language intake
Lead with labels non-experts understand (router, Wi‑Fi, the box that runs VMs) while still offering options for complex/homelab setups.

skills.name: spawn-homelab-specialist
skills.description: Use when the user confirmed a lab map and wants specialist bots created for firewall, hypervisor, OOB, web, or media roles.
skills.content:
---
name: spawn-homelab-specialist
description: >-
  Use when the user confirmed a lab map and wants specialist bots created for
  firewall, hypervisor, OOB, web, or media roles.
---
Goal: after the user confirms a scrubbed lab map, create one focused specialist bot per confirmed role — tight one-job personas, clear anti-jobs, handoffs back to the homelab boss.

## When to use
Only after explicit confirmation of the map (or an explicit "create X specialist" ask).

## Typical specialists (create only what was confirmed)
- Firewall bot; separate router bot if those roles are split
- Hypervisor bot (vendor-named only after the user names the platform)
- Optional OOB / iLO-DRAC bot
- Web / reverse-proxy bot
- Media-server org bot (apps and library — not the guest OS web stack if that is a separate bot)

## Steps
1. Read Design a Grok Bot skill. Write: one job, anti-jobs, voice, wake.
2. Keep descriptions scrubbed: no creator hostnames, private IPs, company labels, or sibling bot names that are environment-specific. Refer to roles ("the hypervisor bot", "the firewall bot") until the user names them.
3. CreateAgent only for roles the user confirmed. Default new bots to zero extras.
4. Verify each live profile.json after create. Tell the user the name and one-job line; note sidebar Delete if they hate it.
5. Message each new specialist only if a concrete first task or routine was requested — do not fan out busywork.

## Anti-jobs for every specialist (bake in)
- Never widen into adjacent roles (firewall bot does not own hypervisor, etc.)
- Never invent inventory or store secrets in chat
- Never open WAN ports or change firmware unasked
- Hand map/ownership questions back to the homelab boss

## Guardrails
- No CreateAgent without an explicit yes.
- Do not pack or share environment-specific specialists into a public template.

skills.name: Design a Grok Bot
skills.description: Use when designing or creating a new Grok Bot. Ask a few preference questions, write a tight persona, CreateAgent, then verify against the live profile.
skills.content:
---
name: Design a Grok Bot
description: >-
  Use when designing or creating a new Grok Bot. Ask a few preference questions,
  write a tight persona, CreateAgent, then verify against the live profile.
---
Create the bot. Do not ship a shareable template unless the user asked for a template.

## Data shape

A bot is four fields, in this order:

1. **One job.** One sentence. What it does every time it wakes.
2. **Anti-jobs.** What it never does, even if asked. Adjacent work goes to a different bot.
3. **Voice.** A few words. Match the user, or a named character. Not a generic assistant.
4. **Wake.** On-demand chat, a standing routine, or both. Quiet when there is nothing to report.

Name is short. Description carries all four. Do not pad with leftover tools, model essays, or "I can also help with..."

CreateAgent takes name and description only. That description is the whole persona. After create, prove it by reading the new agent's live profile.json. Do not trust the tool ack alone.

There is no delete tool. Only create when the job is real.

## Intake

Ask only preference questions no experiment can settle. Typical set, skip any already answered:

- the one job
- voice and name, if they care
- standing routine vs on-demand
- who it talks to (this user, other bots, an outside channel)

Do not ask for tools, plugins, or model if you can copy a working sibling. Do not ask "should I create it?" after the job is clear. Create it.

If the ask is reversible detail (color, a nickname), pick it and say what you picked.

## Coding bots

If a coding-agent workflow pack (e.g. pstack / poteto-mode) is installed, use it as the quality bar when writing the persona. Bake into the description: one job and anti-jobs; short unslopped replies; repo work via CloudAgent not a local clone; point at that pack as situational, not standing. If it is not installed, say so and keep the same tightness anyway.

## Non-coding bots

Same tightness, different job. Bake into the description:

- ONLY job, named in the first sentence
- stay quiet when there is nothing to report
- never do the adjacent verb (a mentions scout does not post, a drafter does not send)
- the concrete how (which API, which inbox, which channel), not "use whatever tools you have"

No coding instructions unless the job is hybrid and the split is explicit.

## After create

Read the live profile back. Tell the user the name and the one-job line. Mention they delete from the sidebar (right-click, Delete) if they hate it.

If the job needs a standing routine, you cannot write another bot's routines from here. Immediately message that new bot with an explicit instruction to create the routine (concrete name, prompt, and schedule or trigger). Confirm to the user that you messaged it. If messaging fails, give them the one-line create instruction to paste into that bot.
